security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel vector-state accessors (ptrace get/set, signal frame marshaling, KVM vreg ioctls) use vmv.x.s/vmv.s.x/vfmv.f.s/vfmv.s.f assuming a single-register operand, but when EEW > VLEN the spec now defines EMUL=ceil(EEW/VLEN) meaning the scalar spans a register group—reading/writing only the lowest-numbered register of the group silently accesses partial or wrong element data
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: vmv\.x\.s|vmv\.s\.x|vfmv\.f\.s|vfmv\.s\.f in arch/riscv/kernel/vector, arch/riscv/kernel/signal, arch/riscv/kvm, arch/riscv/kernel/ptrace without checking that ceil(EEW/VLEN)==1 or without accessing the full register group
security_spec.summary: ELEN>VLEN redefines scalar move and reduction operands from single-register to register-group (EMUL=ceil(EEW/VLEN)); kernel code using these to peek/poke individual elements in ptrace/KVM/signals will corrupt state if EEW>VLEN

findings.finding: Uses vse8.v with fixed e8,m8 to save entire register file as raw bytes. No vmv.x.s/vmv.s.x/vfmv.f.s/vfmv.s.f instructions. EEW/VLEN relationship irrelevant since access is always at byte granularity.
findings.snippet:
vsetvli %0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma
vse8.v v0, (%1)
...
vse8.v v24, (%1)

findings.finding: Uses vle8.v with fixed e8,m8 to restore entire register file as raw bytes. No scalar-register transfer instructions.
findings.snippet:
vsetvli %0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma
vle8.v v0, (%1)
...
vle8.v v24, (%1)

findings.finding: Uses vmv.v.i (vector-vector moves from immediate), not scalar-register transfers. No vmv.x.s/vmv.s.x/vfmv.f.s/vfmv.s.f.
findings.snippet:
vmv.v.i v0, -1
vmv.v.i v8, -1
vmv.v.i v16, -1
vmv.v.i v24, -1

findings.finding: Copies the entire datap buffer as raw bytes via membuf_write. No per-element access via vmv.x.s etc. The EEW>VLEN register-group concern does not apply.
findings.snippet:
membuf_write(&to, &ptrace_vstate, sizeof(struct __riscv_v_regset_state));
return membuf_write(&to, vstate->datap, riscv_v_vsize);

findings.finding: Copies the entire datap buffer as raw bytes via user_regset_copyin. No per-element access. SEW <= ELEN checked in invalid_ptrace_v_csr but no EEW>VLEN guard needed since kernel never does scalar-element extraction.
Copies the entire vstate datap buffer to userspace via __copy_to_user with riscv_v_vsize. No per-element scalar-register access.
Copies the entire vstate datap buffer from userspace via copy_from_user with riscv_v_vsize. No per-element access. No vmv.x.s/vmv.s.x/vfmv.f.s/vfmv.s.f.

Uses copy_to_user of reg_size bytes from the datap buffer. Per-register byte copying via kvm_riscv_vcpu_vreg_addr which computes offset as (reg_num - base) * vlenb. Treats each vector register as vlenb bytes with no element-level access.
Uses copy_from_user of reg_size bytes into the datap buffer. Per-register byte copying with no element-level access. No vmv.x.s/vmv.s.x/vfmv.f.s/vfmv.s.f.
Thin wrapper delegating to __riscv_v_vstate_save which uses vse8.v e8,m8 — full register file save as raw bytes, independent of EEW/VLEN relationship.
Thin wrapper delegating to __riscv_v_vstate_restore which uses vle8.v e8,m8 — full register file restore as raw bytes, independent of EEW/VLEN relationship.
